content:
The datasheet defines **two ordering codes** (footnotes 1) and 2)) with distinct Tx wavelength bands; everything else is shared in one technical row. Do **not** cross-product standards, bit rates, and host interfaces—they all apply to both parts.

```json
{
  "modes": [
    {
      "label": "SO-XFP-10GE-BX40D-2733 BiDi 1270nm Tx / 1330nm Rx",
      "model": "SO-XFP-10GE-BX40D-2733",
      "wavelength_min_nm": 1260.0,
      "wavelength_max_nm": 1280.0,
      "wavelength_center_nm": 1270.0,
      "host_interface_name": ["INF-8077i", "XFP MSA"],
      "standards_code": ["10GBASE-ER", "10GBASE-EW", "10GbE-LAN", "10GbE-WAN", "OTU2", "OTU2e", "STM-64", "OC192"],
      "bit_rate_gbps": [9.95, 11.1, 11.3]
    },
    {
      "label": "SO-XFP-10GE-BX40D-3327 BiDi 1330nm Tx / 1270nm Rx",
      "model": "SO-XFP-10GE-BX40D-3327",
      "wavelength_min_nm": 1320.0,
      "wavelength_max_nm": 1340.0,
      "wavelength_center_nm": 1330.0,
      "host_interface_name": ["INF-8077i", "XFP MSA"],
      "standards_code": ["10GBASE-ER", "10GBASE-EW", "10GbE-LAN", "10GbE-WAN", "OTU2", "OTU2e", "STM-64", "OC192"],
      "bit_rate_gbps": [9.95, 11.1, 11.3]
    }
  ]
}
```

If your validator requires **scalar** fields only, use the same two modes and pick one value per key only where the sheet gives a single binding; for shared multi-valued fields you would need schema support for arrays (or separate mode objects per proven row), not artificial pairings of standard ↔ bit rate.
